record.title: SB 2-D (2026 Special Session D): Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights (passed Senate, died in House)
record.short_title: Florida AI Bill of Rights (SB 2-D, 2026 Special Session D)
record.issuing_body: Florida Senate (2026 Special Session D; sponsor Sen. Brodeur)
record.summary: Would have created an 'Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights'. Companion chatbot platforms would have had to bar minors from accounts without parental consent, give consenting parents controls and self-harm alerts, remind minors hourly that the chatbot is not human, and take reasonable measures against material harmful to minors. Bot operators would have had to tell users hourly that they are not talking to a human, AI companies could sell or disclose users' personal information only as deidentified data, governments could not contract for AI with entities tied to foreign countries of concern, and commercial use of AI-generated likenesses would have needed consent.
record.notes: Filed on 24 Apr 2026 and referred to Rules; on 28 Apr 2026 it was withdrawn from Rules and passed by the Senate 37-1. In the House it was referred to the Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee and died there on 29 Apr 2026, as did the linked public-records bill SB 4-D. It carries the same title as CS/SB 482 of the 2026 Regular Session (US-FL-01), which died in House messages on 13 Mar 2026. The bill stated an effective date of 1 Jul 2026. The Department of Legal Affairs would have enforced the chatbot, bot and data provisions as deceptive or unfair trade practices, with civil penalties of up to USD 50,000 per violation and a discretionary 45-day cure period, and minors could have recovered up to USD 10,000 from a chatbot platform. It would also have barred schools from giving students AI instructional tools before grade 6, with exceptions, and required parental notice and an opt-out.

verification.note: Stored the Florida Senate bill page for SB 2-D (session 2026D), the Senate Rules Committee pre-meeting analysis of 24 Apr 2026 and the Senate floor vote record of 28 Apr 2026 (flsenate.gov). The bill page confirms the title, sponsor, the single filed version, the effective date stated in the bill, the 37-1 Senate vote and the House action 'Died in Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee' on 29 Apr 2026; the vote record confirms the 37-1 vote. The bill passed the Senate without amendments, so the analysis of the filed version, on which the summary rests, describes the text that lapsed. The bill text itself was not stored.

judgment.status_reasoning: The bill passed the Senate 37-1 on 28 Apr 2026 and died in the House Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee on 29 Apr 2026 ('Last Action: 4/29/2026 House - Died in ...'). A bill that died at the end of its session is Proposed with status Lapsed. Its stated effective date (1 Jul 2026) never applied.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope with no scope_note: a pending-then-lapsed AI-specific bill on companion chatbots and minors, bot disclosure, AI companies' data practices, government AI procurement and AI-generated likenesses. Kept as a separate record rather than an update of US-FL-01, because it is a different bill (its own number and history, filed in Special Session D), not a new version of CS/SB 482; linked to US-FL-01.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the filing date (24 Apr 2026), as US-FL-01 uses the filing date of SB 482. There was only one version, so date_last_updated is empty; the passage and death dates are in the notes.
judgment.related_reasoning: US-FL-01 is CS/SB 482 of the 2026 Regular Session with the same title and largely the same subjects (companion chatbots and minors, bot disclosure, government AI contracting).
